claim: The front 'Also' fits も, which I learned in Lesson 4, as well as それから, and nothing separates them.
evidence: Production front: 'Grammar & Function Words / Also' -> それから. Lesson 4 card も: 'Also, too, either (particle)'. The difference (それから joins two sentences, も sits on a noun) is only in the note on the back.
fix: Add a hint such as 'the word that starts a second sentence, not the particle'.
verdictReason: Production front is 'Grammar & Function Words / Also' with no hint. Ledger (chapter-4) teaches も as 'Also, too, either (particle)', so 'Also' has two taught answers; the only thing separating them is the '(particle)' tag on the OTHER card, and the それから note that explains the difference is on the back. Shared rule: when one English shape maps to two structures, the hint names the structure. The book's gloss 'also' is faithful, so the fix is a hint, not an English change.

claim: The front 'Child' is answered by こども, which an earlier card tells me is the ordinary general word for a child.
evidence: Production front: 'Family & People / Child' -> こ (no hint). chapter-9-extras こども: '(My) child', hint 'the word for your own child, and the general word for a child', note 'こども is also the ordinary general word for "child" in any other context.'
fix: Add a hint that it is the short root used in おんなのこ／おとこのこ, e.g. 'the one-syllable word, as in girl and boy'.
verdictReason: Front is 'Family & People / Child' with no hint. chapter-9-extras x9f-kodomo ships English '(My) child' with hint 'the word for your own child, and the general word for a child' and a note saying こども is the ordinary general word for child, so こども is an explicitly sanctioned answer to 'Child'. Only the two cards collide (chapter-24 kodomo is later). A hint naming こ as the short root in おんなのこ／おとこのこ settles it without giving the word away.

claim: This chapter teaches that 'X is at Y' can be said with に あります／います or contracted to です, but only the grammar2 pair carries the hint that says which form is wanted, so the other location cards are a coin toss on Production.
evidence: Unhinted cards: ks4-smith-floor 'Smith-san is on the second floor.' -> ...にいます; fib-hanaya-tonari-byouin 'The florist is next to the hospital.' -> ...にあります; fib-tanakasan-doko-q 'Where is Tanaka-san?' -> どこにいますか; fib-tanakasan-doko-a 'He's in the president's office.' -> しゃちょうしつにいます. Each has an equally correct です form (chapter-13-extras sp-ima-doko-q: 'with a person, the place +です contraction works the same way it does for things'). Hinted cards: grammar2-2, grammar2-3.
fix: Put the grammar2-2 or grammar2-3 hint on every は-topic location card, so the front names the form.
verdictReason: Checked every card named: ks4-smith-floor, fib-hanaya-tonari-byouin, fib-tanakasan-doko-q/-a carry no hint or scene naming the form, while grammar2-2/grammar2-3 split the identical English only by hint, and the deck itself teaches that the です contraction is equally valid (grammar2-3 note; extras sp-ima-doko-q note extends it to people). So the front does not determine に あります／います versus です. Minimal consistent fix: once ks3-taxi-stand is restored to に あります (merged finding), the base unit has no unhinted です card, so hinting only the contracted cards and leaving 'no hint = full に あります／います form' as the deck convention is enough; hinting every card is the thorough alternative.

evidence: fib-meishi-desk-count 'roku-mai' but nanmai card 'nanmai'; fib-fork-table-count-q 'nan-bon' but nanbon card 'nanbon'; fib-fork-table-count-a 'jup-pon'; fib-kumano-chikai-a 'nijup-pun ... Basu de'; fib-kumano-chikai-q 'Kumano-jinja' but kumanojinja card 'kumano jinja'; fib-tanakasan-doko-q 'Tanaka-san' but sorekara-example 'tanaka-san'. Preflight lists only mit-tsu and san-nin here.
fix: Normalise these to the deck's romaji style (no counter hyphens, one casing rule for names).
verdictReason: The inconsistencies are real (verified in cards.json pronunciation fields), but the proposed direction is backwards. The pinned style (src/translate/romajiStyle.js, copied in card-authoring-rules.md) HYPHENATES number+counter (ip-pon, san-gai) and capitalises proper nouns with a hyphenated honorific (Tanaka-san, Kumano-jinja). So roku-mai, nan-bon, jup-pon, nijup-pun, Tanaka-san and Kumano-jinja are the correct spellings; the deviants are the word cards kumanojinja 'kumano jinja', sorekara-example 'tanaka-san', ks4-smith-floor 'sumisu-san', plus 'Basu de' (common noun capitalised after a period) in fib-kumano-chikai-a, and fused gohon/yonin on pen-drawer-example/ks2-guests. nanbon/nanmai (question word + counter) are not covered by the rule; pick one spelling. Preflight lists only mit-tsu and san-nin because casing and the ん apostrophe are deliberately not linted, so this is not a duplicate.

claim: Two 'The X is next to the Y.' cards in this chapter want different endings, and neither front says which.
evidence: Production front: 'Directions / The soba shop is next to the police box.' (no hint) -> そばやはこうばんのとなりです. chapter-13 fib-hanaya-tonari-byouin: 'Shopping / The florist is next to the hospital.' (no hint) -> はなやはびょういんのとなりにあります. ex-parking-next-to-konbini: 'The parking lot is next to the convenience store.' (no hint) -> ...のとなりにあります.
fix: Give this card the 'contracted with です' hint and the にあります cards the 'using に あります' hint.
verdictReason: Verified: 'The soba shop is next to the police box.' → そばやはこうばんのとなりです (no hint); fib-hanaya-tonari-byouin (base) and ex-parking-next-to-konbini (extras) have the same 'The X is next to the Y.' shape → …のとなりにあります, also unhinted. The deck's td-sobaichi pair shows the two forms are treated as different answers. The です form is legitimate (the book's listening cloze VII uses こうばんは ___ です), so the fix is the 'contracted with です' hint on this card, and the に あります hint on the others is optional if 'unhinted = full form' becomes the convention.

claim: 'Where is the boat dock?' wants どこですか while three same-shaped fronts in this unit want どこにありますか, with nothing to tell them apart.

claim: Without a scene I answer with は, the way every adjective sentence since Lesson 10 has gone; the が version is only right as an answer to 'which one is good?', and the front does not say so.
evidence: Production front: 'Food / The bakery's bread is good.' (no scene) -> パンやのパンがおいしいです. The note says が 'picks out whose bread is the good one (NOTES 2)'. Lesson 10 pattern: このほんはおもしろいです. The sobaichi pair in this unit does carry scenes (td-sobaichi-ga-oishii: 'answering "この ちかくに おいしい おそばやさんが ありますか"'; wa-sobaichi-oishii: 'where the shop is already under discussion').
fix: Add a scene such as 'answering which shop's bread is good'.
verdictReason: Verified: scene and hint are both null. NOTES 2 (and the card's own note) says 〜が おいしいです marks the part before が as new information, i.e. an answer to 'which one is good?'. Without that context パンやのパンはおいしいです is the form every adjective sentence since Lesson 10 has used, and the unit's own sobaichi pair (td-sobaichi-ga-oishii, wa-sobaichi-oishii) carries exactly the kind of scene this card lacks. A scene such as 'answering whose bread is the good one' settles it.

claim: 'soba shop' gives me そばや (Lesson 12, and fib-sobaya-kouban-tonari in this unit) but this card wants おそばやさん, and only the word card carries the hint for the polite form.

Is there a good soba shop nearby?' -> すみません。このちかくにおいしいおそばやさんがありますか. chapter-13 osobayasan front: 'Soba shop / polite form, with the honorific お (o) in front and the …さん (san, "Mr./Ms.") ending'. fib-sobaya-kouban-tonari: 'The soba shop is next to the police box.' -> そばや...

The osobayasan word card carries the polite-form hint precisely because 'Soba shop' alone maps to both. claim: The same に あります／です choice runs through this unit: only the two sobaichi location cards say which form they want, so the remaining location statements cannot be answered reliably on Production.

claim: The hint glosses the さん in おそばやさん as the "Mr./Ms." ending, but the book says さん after 〜や only softens the tone.

fix: Reword the hint to say the お in front and the さん ending soften the tone, without the "Mr./Ms." gloss.
verdictReason: NOTES 1: 'Adding the suffix 〜さん after the 〜や denoting shop softens the tone.' The hint glosses the same さん as the 'Mr./Ms.' ending, which the book does not say about this use; the card's own back note already has the right explanation ('softens the tone'). Rewording the hint to keep the cue (お in front, さん at the end, softer/politer) and drop the 'Mr./Ms.' gloss costs nothing and removes the only place the deck frames it as a title. Polish is right.

evidence: Book, EXERCISES II A-2: "A : ( フォーク、なんぼん ) B : (10 ぽん )". Card target: "10ほんあります" (romaji jup-pon arimasu). Other cards spell the change: そのあかワインを１ぽんください, ビールを３ぼんください, バスで20ぷんぐらいです.
fix: Change the target to 10ぽんあります.

Every other number+ほん target in the collection spells the change (chapter-5 counter-hon-10 じゅっぽん, chapter-5-extras １ぽん／３ぼん; pen-drawer-example 5ほん is correctly ごほん). Raised to should-fix: the displayed kana teaches a reading (じゅうほん) that does not exist, and Recognition shows it alone on the front.

claim: GRAMMAR 1 (place に noun が number あります／います, no particle after the number) is shown on several cards but no card's back explains the word order.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1: "the word order is 'place に thing/person が number あります／います.' Also, there is no particle following the number." Cards ks1-chairs, ks2-guests and pen-drawer-example carry no note; only ex-file-drawer-takusan and ni-uketsuke-okyakusan say a number "takes no particle after it", without the order.
fix: Add a note to ks1-chairs giving the order place に thing が number あります and that the number takes no particle, contrasting います on ks2-guests.
verdictReason: GRAMMAR 1 makes two explicit points: the order place に thing/person が number あります／います, and no particle after the number. ks1-chairs, ks2-guests and pen-drawer-example carry no note (checked cards.json), and the ledger with --notes has no earlier card stating that a number+counter takes no particle (Lesson 5's ２ほん note is about the counter's sound; そのワインを２ほんください has no note; the only 'no particle' notes concern time words and ぐらい). The two たくさん notes say 'like a number it takes no particle', presupposing a rule no card has given. A note on ks1-chairs (with the います contrast on ks2-guests) is the fix.

claim: KEY SENTENCE 3 is printed with に あります, the model for GRAMMAR 2, but the card ships the contracted です form.
evidence: Book, KEY SENTENCES 3: "タクシーのりばは えきの まえに あります。" (GRAMMAR 2 cites it as the example of noun は place に あります). Card target: "タクシーのりばはえきのまえです" (takushī noriba wa eki no mae desu).
fix: Change the target to タクシーのりばはえきのまえにあります with romaji takushī noriba wa eki no mae ni arimasu, regenerating its audio.
verdictReason: Book KEY SENTENCES 3 reads タクシーのりばは えきの まえに あります and GRAMMAR 2 cites KS3 as the model for noun は place に あります; EXERCISES III item 1 (タクシーのりば、えきの まえ) drills the same に あります frame. The card ships the contracted です with no hint, so it also collides with wa-kouban-eki-mae (same English shape, に あります). Restoring the book's form fixes both: it matches the book and makes the card consistent with every other unhinted は-topic location card. ttsText/audio must be regenerated (cc7b0c812d772272 is not one of the hand-trimmed clips in .gitignore, so nothing manual is lost).

claim: The card is a が existence sentence but its English is the は-topic translation, the reverse of the mapping GRAMMAR 2 teaches.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 2: "1 かいに レストランが あります。 There is a restaurant on the first floor." vs "レストランは 1 かいに あります。 The restaurant is on the first floor." Card target: "しゃちょうしつのとなりにかいぎしつがあります"; English: "The meeting room is next to the president's office."
fix: Change the English to "There is a meeting room next to the president's office."
verdictReason: GRAMMAR 2 translates ① 1かいに レストランが あります as 'There is a restaurant on the first floor' and ② レストランは 1かいに あります as 'The restaurant is on the first floor', and the deck's own grammar2-1/2-2 and ga-/wa-kouban-eki-mae pairs follow that mapping. This card's target is the が shape with the は-shape English, so a learner applying the deck's rule produces かいぎしつはしゃちょうしつのとなりにあります and is marked wrong. The card is aiSuggested (not a book line), so the English is free to change; 'There is a meeting room next to the president's office.' is the right gloss.
